newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Rescue efforts battle on in snowbound Caucasus.
newsitem.headline: Rescue efforts battle on in snowbound Caucasus.

text.p: Russian emergency workers battled strong winds, blizzards and fog on Friday to clear snowdrifts that have blocked travellers in a road tunnel through the Caucasus mountains for a week.

A spokesman for the Emergencies Ministry in Moscow said some 30 or so drivers remained blocked in the Roksky tunnel, which links Russia with Georgia through the 3,000-metre (10,000-foot) Roksky Pass and which has been cut off by avalanches.

The vast majority of over 200 people trapped last Friday were freed from the tunnel on New Year's Day. Better weather had allowed most of them to be airlifted to the regional centre of Vladikavkaz on Friday.
However, about 30 lorry drivers had opted to stay with their loads and had been provided with food, clothing and medical supplies.
Bulldozers were at work clearing the road to the tunnel on the Russian side. The snow was lying up to 12 metres (40 feet) deep in places, the spokesman said.

Russia's Itar-Tass news agency reported from the Georgian capital Tbilisi that road clearance was also under way on the other side of the range, notably on the Krestovy Pass which straddles the main highway from Tbilisi to Vladikavkaz.
The agency quoted Russian officials as saying forecasts of warmer weather had raised fears of more avalanches and patrols were out firing anti-aircraft guns to dislodge menacing build-ups of snow.

Tass said on Monday that two women had given birth while trapped in the Roksky Tunnel and one new-born child had died of the cold. Two other people were reported to have died in the area at the weekend.
